project_summary: Unified agent connector gateway and secure credential vault bridging autonomous agents to social apps and outbound workplace channels

problem.label: Problem & User Pain
problem.summary: Autonomous agents lack a unified, secure egress and ingress bridge, causing fragmented credentials management, leaked OAuth tokens, and fragile custom integrations across social platforms and enterprise services.
edge_cases: Agent compromises or prompt injections attempting to extract raw third-party access tokens or OAuth refresh credentials directly via tool calls.
Downstream platform API schema drift or sudden credential expiration during an active multi-step autonomous agent workflow.

scope.label: Scope & Non-Goals
scope.summary: Deliver a unified bidirectional bridge supporting outbound egress tool invocation across social and enterprise APIs, secure credential vaulting, and inbound webhook event normalization into agent SSE streams; non-goals include LLM orchestration, model hosting, or general ETL data pipelines.
edge_cases: High-frequency inbound webhook bursts (e.g. Slack mentions flood or GitHub push storms) overwhelming agent SSE listeners.
Agent attempting destructive administrative actions outside its assigned scoped permission policy.

memory.label: State, Memory & Agent Communication
memory.summary: Zero-overhead encrypted SQLite WAL database managing per-agent credentials, scoped permissions, and event logs with just-in-time AES-256-GCM token decryption and single-flight token rotation.
edge_cases: Multiple concurrent agent threads attempting to read/write credentials during an active OAuth token expiration window.
Master encryption key rotation requiring re-encryption of all stored channel secrets without downtime.

bottlenecks.label: Bottlenecks & Failure Modes
bottlenecks.summary: Downstream platform API rate limiting (HTTP 429s), token expiration cascades, network latency jitter, and unhandled tool error propagation are prevented via token-bucket throttlers and normalized JSON error structures.
edge_cases: Sudden burst of 50+ concurrent agent tool dispatches hitting Twitter/X API tier limits, requiring queuing with exponential jitter backoff.
Downstream service outage (e.g. Slack API degradation returning 503) intercepted and formatted as recoverable retryable errors rather than unhandled socket crashes.

differentiation.label: Prior-Art Differentiation
differentiation.summary: Unlike general workflow automation platforms like n8n-io/n8n or monolithic CLI tools like google-gemini/gemini-cli, ClawBridge is a dedicated zero-trust egress and ingress gateway leveraging modelcontextprotocol/servers to isolate raw credentials from agents while providing robust error recovery and rate-limiting.
edge_cases: Agent requesting batch operations across multiple platforms (e.g. cross-posting an announcement to Twitter, Slack, and LinkedIn simultaneously) with partial failure isolation.
Migration of existing agent integrations from raw platform REST clients to ClawBridge's normalized MCP tool schema without breaking agent prompts.

tooling_recommendations.purpose: Exposes standardized MCP tool schemas (stdio and SSE) for autonomous agents to discover and invoke downstream actions without custom API wrappers.
tooling_recommendations.recommended: FastMCP / Model Context Protocol Python SDK
tooling_recommendations.why: Standardizes agent integration across diverse platforms (NemoClaw, OpenClaw, Muse, Gemini) with zero custom protocol glue.
tooling_recommendations.alternatives: Custom REST/GraphQL APIs (rejected because every agent would require custom client tool definitions rather than native MCP compatibility).

tooling_recommendations.purpose: Zero-overhead local encrypted store for per-agent credentials, platform OAuth tokens, audit logs, and inbound webhook event queues.
tooling_recommendations.why: Ensures zero external infrastructure dependencies for local developers while securing tokens at rest with AES-GCM envelope encryption.
tooling_recommendations.alternatives: HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager (rejected for MVP due to external operational overhead and cloud lock-in).

tooling_recommendations.purpose: Manages OAuth 1.0a and OAuth 2.0 token refreshes, PKCE authorization flows, and JWT validation for third-party platforms.
tooling_recommendations.why: Handles tricky multi-provider OAuth refresh lifecycles automatically to avoid mid-session 401 expiration failures.
tooling_recommendations.alternatives: Custom OAuth refresh loops (rejected as error-prone across differing provider specs like Twitter vs Slack vs Jira).

tooling_recommendations.purpose: Containerizes the ClawBridge server and SQLite database for portable local daemon or cloud deployment.
tooling_recommendations.why: Enables one-command spun up service accessible over stdio or Docker bridge network for multi-agent clusters.
tooling_recommendations.alternatives: Bare-metal process running on host OS (rejected due to Python environment conflicts and permission isolation).

memory_architecture.agent_communication_pattern: Agents communicate with ClawBridge via JSON-RPC 2.0 (Model Context Protocol stdio/SSE) and REST with Bearer tokens; ClawBridge dispatches authenticated HTTP/2 requests to platform APIs.
memory_architecture.workflow_memory_flow: Credentials, OAuth tokens, and audit receipts are stored in an encrypted SQLite database using WAL mode; tokens are decrypted just-in-time for downstream dispatch; inbound events append to an indexed event log and push to connected agent SSE event queues.
memory_architecture.rationale: Transactional SQLite with WAL mode provides embedded zero-overhead ACID transactions, robust single-writer concurrent reads, and zero external infrastructure dependencies, superior to complex distributed databases for local/containerized agent bridges.
memory_architecture.alternatives_considered: External HashiCorp Vault (rejected for MVP due to heavy operational setup overhead); Raw environment variables or plain JSON config files (rejected due to severe credential leakage risks and inability to support live automated token refresh).
failure_modes: Database locking contention (SQLITE_BUSY) under concurrent agent bursts, mitigated by enabling WAL mode, a 5000ms busy timeout, and a thread-safe connection pool.
Token refresh race conditions where multiple parallel agent requests trigger simultaneous OAuth token refresh calls, mitigated by single-flight mutex locking per channel credentials.

red_team_critiques.title: OAuth Token Refresh Stampede
red_team_critiques.attack: When multiple agents simultaneously dispatch requests through an expired OAuth token, concurrent refresh requests hit the identity provider (e.g. Slack/X), invalidating the refresh token and locking out all agents.
red_team_critiques.mitigation: Implement single-flight distributed mutex per credential ID in memory so only one refresh call executes while others await the updated access token.

red_team_critiques.title: Inbound Webhook Replay & Spoofing
red_team_critiques.attack: An adversary intercepts a valid webhook from Jira or Slack and replays it repeatedly, triggering costly automated agent loops or unauthorized state changes.
red_team_critiques.mitigation: Enforce platform HMAC-SHA256 signature verification, a strict 300-second timestamp freshness window, and SQLite-backed deduplication on webhook delivery IDs.

red_team_critiques.title: Agent Privilege Escalation via Unscoped Tool Dispatch
red_team_critiques.attack: A lightweight agent (e.g. read-only social monitor) invokes destructive tools (e.g. Jira issue deletion or Slack workspace admin endpoints) using the shared bridge.
red_team_critiques.mitigation: Enforce per-agent Access Control Lists (ACLs) mapped to Agent Identity tokens, rejecting unauthorized tool calls before platform dispatch.

system_design.sequence_mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Agent as Autonomous Agent (e.g. NemoClaw)
    participant Gateway as ClawBridge MCP Gateway
    participant Vault as Encrypted Vault (SQLite WAL)
    participant API as External Platform (e.g. Slack / Jira)

    Note over Agent,Gateway: Outbound Tool Invocation Flow
    Agent->>Gateway: tools/call (slack_post_message, args, agent_token)
    Gateway->>Gateway: Validate Agent Identity & ACL Policy
    Gateway->>Gateway: Check Channel Rate Limiter
    Gateway->>Vault: Fetch Channel OAuth Token (JIT Decrypt)
    alt Token Expired?
        Vault->>API: Single-Flight OAuth Refresh Request
        API-->>Vault: Return Fresh Access Token
        Vault->>Vault: Store Re-Encrypted Token
    end
    Gateway->>API: POST /api/chat.postMessage (Bearer Token)
    alt Downstream Success
        API-->>Gateway: HTTP 200 {ok: true, ts: "..."}
        Gateway-->>Agent: tool_result {status: "success", receipt: {...}}
    else Downstream Rate Limited (429)
        API-->>Gateway: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests (Retry-After: 10)
        Gateway-->>Agent: tool_result {status: "error", code: "RATE_LIMITED", retry_after_s: 10}
    end

    Note over Gateway,Agent: Inbound Webhook Event Flow
    API-->>Gateway: Inbound Webhook (HMAC Header, Payload)
    Gateway->>Gateway: Verify HMAC Signature & Freshness (<300s)
    Gateway->>Vault: Deduplicate Delivery ID
    Gateway-->>Agent: Push Event via SSE topic (channel_mention)

options_matrix.pros: Raw secrets never touch LLM context, unified tool schema
options_matrix.cons: Gateway becomes single point of failure

options_matrix.pros: Simple implementation, agents make direct HTTP calls
options_matrix.cons: Massive security risk, token leakage in prompts, fragmented refresh logic

options_matrix.pros: Zero external infrastructure dependencies, fast local ACID transactions
options_matrix.cons: Requires manual replication if clustering across multiple machines

options_matrix.pros: Enterprise HA and centralized key management
options_matrix.cons: Heavy operational overhead and high barrier for local agent development

implementation_steps: Step 1: Core Encrypted SQLite Vault & Credentials Model :: Schema, AES-256-GCM envelope encryption, Authlib OAuth token model, and migrations ::
Step 2: Agent Identity & Scoped Access Control Layer :: Agent token generation, authentication middleware, and per-tool granular ACL enforcement :: Step 1
Step 3: Outbound Egress Dispatcher & Token-Bucket Rate Limiter :: HTTP/2 client with JIT token attachment, exponential backoff, and error normalizer :: Step 2
Step 4: FastMCP Server & Tool Definitions :: Model Context Protocol server exposing Slack, Jira, Twitter/X, and Discord tool actions :: Step 3
Step 5: Inbound Webhook Receiver & SSE Event Stream :: HMAC signature validation, delivery deduplication, and agent-subscribed SSE event topics :: Step 4
Step 6: End-to-End Verification & Multi-Agent Test Harness :: Automated integration test suite validating NemoClaw/OpenClaw simulation calls :: Step 5
